sample_unit: expert response-pair ratings (4 experts x 10 FAQ x 2 sources)

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot and gold-standard brachytherapy answers versus recommended level
links.effect: Both sources significantly exceeded recommended reading levels (>12th grade Flesch-Kincaid); AI responses substantially longer; simulated patients rated readability easy for 44% of AI vs 92% of GS responses.
links.quote: Objective analysis confirmed that both sources significantly exceeded the recommended reading levels (e.g., >12th grade Flesch-Kincaid), with AI responses being substantially longer.

links.outcome: Chatbot helpfulness and readability for simulated patient personas of varying literacy
links.effect: Simulated patients preferred GS responses (62% vs 34%), particularly lower-literacy personas; readability easy/very easy 92% for GS vs 44% for AI.
links.quote: Simulated patients preferred GS responses (62% vs. 34%), particularly lower-literacy personas, citing better perceived readability (92% easy/very easy vs. 44% for AI) and a more reassuring tone (42% vs. 24% for AI).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT 4o-mini answering brachytherapy FAQs evaluated by clinician experts and simulated patient personas, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
